one_liner: Header-only C FFT with an FFTW-shaped API and minfft-style split-radix core; 8-13% faster than minfft on ARM, far behind FFTW.
what_it_does: A single-header C library (C++ wrapper in notorious_fft.hpp) for complex and real DFTs in 1-D to N-D, DCT/DST types 2-4, at any length, in double precision by default or float with NOTORIOUS_FFT_SINGLE. It offers two APIs: minfft-style aux objects (notorious_fft_mkaux_dft_1d plus notorious_fft_dft(x, y, aux)) and an FFTW-shaped planner (notorious_fft_plan_dft_1d / execute / destroy_io_plan). An optional notorious_fft_fftw.h maps a subset of fftw_* names (1-3D dft, r2c/c2r, r2r_1d, rank-1 plan_many_dft, malloc/free) onto it by macro. Inverses are unnormalized and the data layout matches FFTW's.
how_it_is_fast: Powers of two use a recursive split-radix 2/4 decimation-in-frequency kernel with unrolled terminals for N <= 32 and no bit-reversal pass; header comments say it uses the same structure and twiddle layout as minfft's rs_dft_1d. Under MEASURE planning it may instead pick a DIT combine or iterative Cooley-Tukey, and it switches to a four-step algorithm at N >= 2^20. Factors 3/5/7 are peeled by mixed-radix passes, primes with 7-smooth N-1 use Rader, and other lengths use Bluestein. Compile-time NEON, AVX2 and AVX-512 paths exist (the README's summary lists NEON for f64 and f32, AVX2 for the inverse and AVX-512 for the forward transform), and each plan's memory is one 64-byte-aligned slab.
when_to_use: You already use minfft and want a near drop-in with more transform types and arbitrary lengths: same aux-object calling style, 1.08-1.13x faster complex DFTs at N >= 256 on a Cortex-A78AE
Embedded or edge aarch64 (Jetson-class) code that wants one MIT header with no dependencies beyond libc and libm
Prototyping against an FFTW-like API with a permissive license, for a subset of FFTW calls, when FFTW-level speed is not required
Small DCT-2/3/4 or DST-2/3/4 transforms where a header-only implementation is more convenient than linking a library
when_not_to_use: As an FFTW replacement for speed: in the author's FastAndFourier benchmarks on an x86 AVX2 Mac (Feb 2026, older build, one run, -ffast-math) it ran at 0.57-0.76x of KissFFT's throughput and 10x-30x slower than FFTW_MEASURE (e.g. N=1024 45.7 us vs 1.79 us; ratios derived from page data)
x86 users who need published numbers: only an ARM Cortex-A78AE table exists for this repository; the AVX2/AVX-512 paths have no results
Small real transforms and DCT-2 at N=16-64, where it was 0.83-0.97x of minfft's speed
Projects needing a mature dependency: 7 commits, 0 stars, no releases on GitHub, and a Bluestein AVX inverse bug fixed only on 2026-08-22, after v1.0.0
Calling one plan from several threads at once: plans own scratch buffers, so concurrent execute on the same plan is unsupported

integration.dependencies: none at runtime (libc, libm); OpenMP optional and switched on by default in the CMake build; the bundled tests and benchmarks fetch minfft (master) via FetchContent; Python 3 is needed by CMake to regenerate the amalgamated header
integration.min_toolchain: C11 (C++17 for the C++ wrapper and tests), CMake 3.14+
integration.platforms: any C11 target with a scalar path; NEON on aarch64/ARMv7, AVX2+FMA or AVX-512F/DQ on x86-64, all chosen at compile time from compiler flags (no runtime dispatch)
integration.thread_safety: Documented: concurrent execute on the same plan is not supported (plans own scratch); distinct plans may run in parallel
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — notorious_fft_fftw.h aliases a subset of the FFTW3 API by macro (no wisdom, no guru interface, plan_many_dft fully only for rank 1), and must not be combined with linking libfftw3 in the same translation unit

gotchas: Precision is a build-wide switch: in the FFTW compatibility header fftwf_complex is typedef'd to the same type as fftw_complex, so float and double FFTW code cannot coexist in one build
NOTORIOUS_FFT_FAST_MATH swaps in Bhaskara I sin/cos approximations with ~0.1% twiddle error that grows with N; the README also warns against -ffast-math
Multi-dimensional c2r / invrealdft may overwrite its input
CMake regenerates include/notorious_fft.h in the source tree from the src/ modules whenever they change, and the published minfft comparison builds against minfft master without a pinned commit
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over minfft when you want the same small-library style plus non-power-of-two sizes, DCT/DST variants and an FFTW-like planner; for speed, PocketFFT, PFFFT or muFFT are better-measured permissive choices, and FFTW was 10x-30x faster on x86 in the author's own sibling benchmark.
verified_claims_summary: The repository's bench.c times notoriousfft against minfft in one binary (CLOCK_MONOTONIC, two warm-up calls, one timed batch of 500-100,000 repetitions per size, minfft run first), built with GCC 11.4.0 -O3 for armv8.2-a on a Jetson Orin Cortex-A78AE in double precision. v1.0.0 was 1.08-1.13x faster on forward complex DFT for N >= 256 (N=4096: 68.95 us vs 77.59 us), up to 1.18x on inverse, 1.01-1.07x on real DFT, and slightly slower at N=16 for real DFT and DCT-2; with a single timed batch, margins under ~5% are within run-to-run noise.
status_note: Young single-author project (7 commits, 2026-02-20 to 2026-08-22, 0 stars, MIT); small enough to vendor as one header, but treat it as experimental and expect FFTW-class libraries to be much faster on x86.
